name: CH32X035G8U6
title: 32-bit RISC-V microcontroller with USB full-speed host/device and USB PD/Type-C
summary: CH32X035 and CH32X033 are industrial-grade 48 MHz microcontrollers on the QingKe RISC-V4C core, with 62 KB flash and 20 KB SRAM, running from 2 V to 5.5 V on the internal 48 MHz RC oscillator. The CH32X035 carries USB full-speed host and device and a USB PD/Type-C controller, each with its PHY. Around the core: a 12-bit ADC with touch-key sensing, two op-amps/PGAs, up to three comparators, four USARTs, I2C, SPI, two advanced and one general timer, 8-channel DMA and a small programmable I/O processor (PIOC) for one- and two-wire protocols. The family spans LQFP64M down to QFN12; the CH32X035G8U6 is the QFN28.
key_figures: 2.0 V to 5.5 V (3.0 V to 5.3 V with USB or PD)
4.2 mA typ at 48 MHz, 3.3 V, all peripherals on
51 µA typ, IWDG and AWU off

notes: OPA and CMP count units; ADC channels are external plus one internal.

tables.title: Pin definitions, CH32X035
notes: Type: I is a TTL/CMOS Schmitt input, O a CMOS three-state output, A an analog input or output, P power.
A remap function's suffix after the underscore is the value of its field in the AFIO register: TX2_2 means the field is set to 10b.
ADC channels 3, 7, 11 and 15 (A3, A7, A11) and every I2C function (SCL, SDA and their remaps) do not work on devices whose lot number has 0 as its fifth character from the end.

On every CH32X033 and CH32X035 device except CH32X035F8U6 and CH32X035D8U6, PC10 is joined to PC17 and PC11 to PC16 inside the package; neither pair may have both pins set as outputs, and in USB use PC10 and PC11 stay floating inputs (their reset state).
CH32X035G8U6 and CH32X035G8R6: PB1 and PB5 share one pin inside; never both outputs.
CH32X035G8R6: PA12 shares a pin with PC14, and PA13 with PC15; never both outputs.
CH32X035D8U6: PA7 shares a pin with PC7; never both outputs.
PC17 is the boot pin: high at power-up starts the chip from the BOOT area.
PC16 needs an external pull-up resistor in I2C use.
PC3 has the RST function on the QSOP28 and TSSOP20 packages only.
Not every function exists on every part number: the part-number table gives each device's peripherals.

operation.text: QingKe RISC-V4C core running RV32IMAC plus vendor extensions. It has machine and user privilege levels, standard memory protection, static or dynamic branch prediction with conflict handling, single-cycle multiply and a hardware divider, a hardware interrupt stack and the fast programmable interrupt controller PFIC. Debug is the 2-wire SDI interface.
The core, the arbiter, DMA and SRAM talk over several buses: an I-code and a D-code bus to flash, and a system bus to SRAM and the HB peripheral bus. DMA and the CPU reach SRAM through the arbiter.

A small single-cycle RISC core with its own reduced instruction set, clocked at the system clock. It has a 2K-instruction program ROM held in 4K bytes borrowed from system SRAM, 49 SFRs, a PWM timer/counter and a 6-level stack, and offers one 33-byte bidirectional register and one 33-byte one-way register. It drives two I/O pins (PIOC_IO0 on PC18, PIOC_IO1 on PC19, IO0 also remappable to PC7). Loading a different program implements a different one-wire or two-wire protocol; the program can be paused and reloaded at run time.

20K bytes of SRAM, lost at power-off, of which 4K can serve the PIOC. 62K bytes of Code FLASH for the application and constants. 3328 bytes of System FLASH hold the bootloader; with the WCH-LinkUtility tool this area can be added to the user area. 256 bytes of vendor configuration bytes are fixed at the factory; 256 bytes of user option bytes are free for the user's settings.

One supply, VDD = 2 V to 5.5 V, feeds the I/O pins and the internal regulator. VDD must be at least 2.5 V when the ADC or PD is used, and 3.0 V to 5.3 V with USB or PD. The I/O output high level follows VDD, so changing VDD sets the interface level.

Power-on and power-down reset (POR/PDR) is always on: the chip is held in reset while VDD is below VPOR/PDR (about 1.8 V rising, 1.78 V falling) and runs once the supply is above 2 V, with no outside reset circuit. The programmable voltage detector (PVD), enabled in software, compares VDD with one of four thresholds (about 2.1, 2.3, 3 or 4 V) and can raise an interrupt on a falling or rising crossing.
The internal regulator starts after reset. It runs in normal mode while the core runs and drops to a low-power mode in Standby.

Sleep stops only the CPU clock; peripherals keep running, and any interrupt or wake-up event exits it in about 1 µs. Stop puts the flash in low-power mode and turns off the HSI RC oscillator. Standby also puts the regulator in power-saving mode. Stop and Standby exit on any EXTI interrupt or event (one of 24 external I/O lines, the PVD output, USB wake-up, USB PD wake-up), an external reset on RST, or an IWDG reset; wake-up takes about 10 µs. After a wake-up from a mode with clocks off, the internal RC oscillator starts first.

Up to 255 vectors; 7 core interrupts and 39 peripheral interrupts are used. Two interrupts can be masked individually; one NMI; hardware prologue/epilogue (HPE) with no instruction overhead; 4 vector-table-free (VTF) fast interrupts; a vector table in address or instruction form; nesting up to 2 levels; tail chaining. PFIC registers can be reached in user and machine mode.
28 edge detectors, each with its own rising, falling or both-edge trigger and its own mask, and a pending register. Any of the up to 60 GPIOs can be routed to the 24 external interrupt lines.

8 channels with circular-buffer support, for memory-to-memory, peripheral-to-memory and memory-to-peripheral transfers, each channel with its own request logic, priority, length and addresses. Served peripherals: TIMx, ADC, USART, I2C, SPI. USB and USB PD have their own DMA.

The only system clock source is the internal 48 MHz RC oscillator (HSI), on by default. After reset, or with no clock set up, the CPU runs from HSI divided by 6. The HB prescaler divides SYSCLK by 1 to 256 to give HCLK; the core SysTick takes HCLK/8; the ADC clock has its own divider CLK_DIV[3:0]; HSI/1024 clocks the AWU and IWDG; USBFS takes its 48 MHz straight from HSI. MCO[1:0] puts a clock on the MCO pin (PB9). Each peripheral group has its own clock enable.

12-bit ADC with up to 14 external channels and one internal channel, the internal reference VREFINT. Sampling time is programmable per channel; modes are single, continuous, scan and discontinuous. An analog watchdog watches one or more channels. Conversions can start from on-chip timer signals or external pins and can use DMA. The touch-key unit has up to 14 channels sharing the ADC's external inputs; the ADC converts the result and a library routine or the user's code decides the key state. Channels 3, 7, 11 and 15 do not work on lots whose lot number has 0 as its fifth character from the end.

The input is a sampling switch RADC into the 21 pF hold capacitor CADC, with clamp diodes to VDD and GND. Pad and board parasitic capacitance Cp, about 5 pF, adds to it and depends on layout; a larger Cp costs accuracy, and lowering fADC recovers it. The source resistance limit is the RAIN equation.

16-bit up/down auto-reload counters with a 16-bit prescaler, four channels, three of them with complementary outputs, dead-time insertion, a repetition counter and an emergency break input: a three-phase PWM generator for motor control. They link with the other timers for synchronisation or event chaining. TIM2 channels 1 to 3 can be triggered straight from the comparators.
16-bit up-counting auto-reload counter with a 16-bit prescaler and two channels for input capture, output compare, PWM and one-pulse output. It can be frozen in debug mode.

The independent watchdog is a free-running 12-bit down-counter on HSI/1024 with 7 prescaler values; it runs apart from the main program and is started by software or, through the option bytes, by hardware. The window watchdog is a 7-bit down-counter on the main clock with an early-warning interrupt. Both reset the system on a fault and both can be frozen in debug mode.
The core has a 64-bit up or down counter with auto-reload and a selectable clock source, raising the SYSTICK exception (number 12) for an RTOS tick or used as a plain counter.

Four USARTs: full-duplex asynchronous, synchronous one-way and single-wire half-duplex, LIN, ISO7816 smart card, IrDA SIR, CTS/RTS hardware flow control and multiprocessor communication, with a fractional baud-rate generator and DMA. The QFN20, TSSOP20 (CH32X035F7P6) and QFN12 parts have three.

One SPI, master or slave, switchable at run time, multi-master, full or half duplex, with basic SD/MMC modes, programmable clock polarity and phase, 8- or 16-bit frames, hardware CRC and DMA. Up to 24 MHz in either role.

One I2C, multi-master or slave, standard and fast speeds, 7- or 10-bit addressing with dual addresses in 7-bit slave mode, hardware CRC and DMA. It does not work on lots whose lot number has 0 as its fifth character from the end. On PC16 it needs an outside pull-up.

USB 2.0 full-speed host and device controller with its PHY, with BC charging-protocol support, 8 configurable device endpoints and one set of host endpoints, control, bulk, isochronous and interrupt transfers, double buffering, suspend/resume and standby/wake-up. D+ is PC17 (UDP), D- is PC16 (UDM). USB host is on the LQFP64M, LQFP48, QFN28 and QSOP28 parts only.

A USB Power Delivery controller and PHY on CC1 (PC14) and CC2 (PC15): Type-C attach detection, BMC coding and CRC in hardware, hardware edge control, PD 2.0 and PD 3.0, fast charging, sink (UFP), source (DFP) and DRP roles, and PDUSB. The CC pull-up current is selectable at 80, 180 or 330 µA. Adding the CH211 Type-C/PD high-voltage interface chip gives a direct 28 V supply, an internal charge pump driving an N-MOSFET, 28 V tolerance on the CC pins and the switchable 5.1 kΩ Rd pull-down the Type-C specification defines. The CH32X033 has no PD.

Three ports, up to 60 pins. Each pin is an output, an input with or without pull-up (pull-down on some), or a peripheral function. All pins have a switchable pull-up; only PA0-PA15 and PC16-PC17 have a switchable pull-down. PC14-PC17 have extra pull-up modes set in the PD and USB control registers. All PA and PB pins have the stronger drive. A lock mechanism freezes the I/O configuration. A GPIO can sink or source up to ±8 mA, within the absolute maximum totals.

Two op-amps, each also usable as a comparator, with several selectable inputs, a programmable-gain mode (PGA, gains 4, 8, 16, 32) and two selectable outputs, which connect internally to ADC channels so a small signal can be amplified before conversion.

Three rail-to-rail comparators with optional hysteresis, each with two input channels per side and an optional shared reference pin. The output goes to a GPIO or straight to TIM2 CH1 to CH3. CH32X035G8U6 has one comparator.
The 2-wire serial debug interface uses SWDIO (PC18) and SWCLK (PC19). It is on after power-up or reset; the application can turn it off.
PC17 is read at power-up: high starts the chip from the BOOT area (the bootloader in System FLASH).

On the small packages two I/Os can share one pin: PC10 with PC17 and PC11 with PC16 on every part except CH32X035F8U6 and CH32X035D8U6; PB1 with PB5 on CH32X035G8U6 and G8R6; PA12 with PC14 and PA13 with PC15 on G8R6; PA7 with PC7 on D8U6; PA7 with PB0 on CH32X033F8P6. Never set both I/Os of a pair as outputs. In USB use PC10 and PC11 stay floating inputs.

Voltages are referred to GND. Min and max hold over the worst ambient temperature, supply and clock; typical values are at 25 °C and VDD = 5 V. Values from characterisation or design are not tested in production; min and max from characterisation come from sample statistics.

Supply current is measured in series with VDD at room temperature, VDD = 3.3 V, every I/O as an input with pull-up and HSI = 48 MHz, with all peripheral clocks on or all off. Pins not bonded out on the small packages, and bonded pins left unused, should be set as inputs with pull-up or pull-down, or the current rises.
Dimensions are in mm. Lead pitch is exact; every other dimension holds to ±0.2 mm or ±10 %, whichever is larger.
